correctness.rationale: Each fixed positive task multiplier cancels exactly in the normalized gradient and current-to-initial norm ratio. The common target magnitude therefore changes by an explicit probability-weighted arithmetic mean. The source rotation target is normalized and invariant, while the unnormalized rotated task gradient makes the rotation loss and its gradient homogeneous of degree one in the task scale. Common scaling multiplies every source first-order update gradient by the same factor, proving the reciprocal-learning-rate trajectory equivalence by induction.

value.rationale: RotoGrad's defining contribution is to couple magnitude homogenization with slowly learned task-specific rotations. The theorem separates exactly which parts are loss-unit invariant and which are not: the backbone direction is invariant, the shared magnitude follows an arithmetic mean of task units, and rotation/head learning speeds inherit individual task units. This distinction directly affects interpretation of gradient homogenization and the practical leader-follower learning-rate separation.
